title: Why every country wants its own AI, and what that means for your business
youtube_title: Why every country wants its own AI, and what it means for the AI you use
youtube_description:
Why every country wants its own AI

Every AI has two passports: where it was born and where it lives. The first shapes what it tells you. The second decides who sees your data.

I put the same work questions to Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek, changing only the country. On a supplier with cotton from Xinjiang, DeepSeek wrote a full answer, deleted it and changed the subject. Every time.

My call: a Chinese AI is fine if you don't mind where your data ends up. Just check what it tells you.

linkedin_post:
Airbnb's boss said its customer service AI relies a lot on Qwen, a Chinese AI. Lindy moved its AI work to DeepSeek, and its boss said DeepSeek was ten times cheaper. Cheap is a fair reason.

But every AI has two passports. Where it was born shapes what it tells you. Where it lives decides who sees your data.

I gave Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek the same question about a supplier's cotton from Xinjiang. DeepSeek wrote a full answer, deleted it and changed the subject. Every time.

Three things I'd do this week:
1. Ask your main software suppliers which AI their product runs on, and where it runs.
2. Put your own work questions to your team's AI and to one from another country, and see where they differ.
3. Keep a second AI ready, so one supplier never has you stuck.

The full piece, with sources, is at makeyourmindup.ai
